summary: Promote Sarah Carter’s existing profile to an individual historian entry, with three specific contributions on reserve agriculture, gender/marriage and women’s land claims. Add carefully credited collaborative bibliography and seven writing/edition facts. Preserve collective field comparisons and original source qualifications while appending bounded primary readings.
authorization: User said continue, then directed that historians and theory be separated, that 150 be the Canadian-history screening threshold, and specifically that Sarah Carter be added. Coordinator assigned this bounded person-entry packet; no publication authorization.
rationale: Carter’s user-requested inclusion leads to researched historical content rather than an automatic citation ranking. The selected primary prefaces/openings and author interview support three distinct contributions. Treaty 7 Elders and Tribal Council retain first collective credit with all three named collaborators; Recollecting retains Carter/McCormack co-editorship and contributor ownership. Book publication, later printings and the corrected 2018 copy stay separate. New source addenda preserve original metadata-only statements and explain exactly what is newly read. No authority merge, Indigenous-identity inference, causal influence claim, automatic dissertation bridge, group review-year change or career interval.

strand.title: Prairie women, colonial imagery, marriage and land
strand.focus: Carter’s studies distinguish the production of racialized femininity, the legal and social imposition of marriage norms, and women’s efforts to acquire land. Gendered exclusion did not place settler and Indigenous women in the same position; the read openings also retain contestation and limits to official power.
strand.works: Capturing Women (1997), preface; The Importance of Being Monogamous (2008), opening; Imperial Plots (2016; corrected reprint 2018), introduction
